_comment: The matrix layer -- the code that decides which access appears in the matrix once inheritance, context rollups and attribute cuts are applied. Chosen as the next scope because it is the closest analogue of the two worst surprises measured so far: src/effectiveAccess/engine.js read 93% line coverage and scored 69% under mutation, src/accountlinking/classifier.js read 97% and scored 68%. Six of these eight files sit at 100% line coverage with their own dedicated test file, which is the same profile, and inheritedAccess.js decides whether a grant is shown as held directly or through a group -- a wrong answer there is silent in both directions and is exactly what a reviewer reads off the matrix. Run: cd app/api && npm run test:mutation:matrix. TEST INCLUDE IS WIDER THAN src/matrix -- see vitest.stryker.matrix.config.js for why: most of these modules are also driven through the route layer, and excluding those tests would manufacture false survivors. MUTATOR SET: StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral excluded, matching every other API config. They were enabled for the first measurements and did pay here -- these tests assert on the emitted SQL, so a mutated literal changes text a test pins and dies, which is the opposite of permissions.js where the strings were prose and 68 of 72 survived. But that yield is mostly one-off, while the cost recurs on every weekly run: string/object mutants were 291 of 1,122 here, 26% of the work. The assertions written to kill them stay and keep earning; only the weekly re-measuring of them stops. Note the score RISES on exclusion, 80.93 -> 83.79, because those mutants were killed at a lower rate than the rest -- read the floor below as measured over a smaller mutant set, not as an improvement. Two files move most: contextRollup.js 68.80 -> 82.76 and attributeCut.js 70.93 -> 74.24, which says most of what was unkilled in them was text. 83.79 is a re-run, not arithmetic on the old report: deriving it by dropping string mutants from the previous report gave 83.39, and up to 3 points out per file, so excluding a mutator does not simply subtract its mutants. Carry this caveat regardless: pinning SQL text proves it is unchanged, not that the query returns the right rows. Query correctness is the contract tests' job. MEASURED 63.44% AT A SUITE LINE COVERAGE OF 94.3% -- the widest coverage-to-fault-detection gap recorded in this repo, and the reason this scope was picked. rollupBuilders.js is the sharpest case: 100% of lines, 100% of branches and 100% of functions, and 38% of injected faults still go unnoticed. THE INCLUDE SET IS NOT THE CAUSE: running the full API suite with coverage limited to src/matrix reproduces these per-file figures exactly (94.26% lines / 76.24% branch, same uncovered lines), so the 103 no-coverage mutants are real gaps, not tests this config left out. FLOOR ratchets up only -- 61 -> 65 -> 70 -> 78 as the scope went 63.44 -> 67.02 -> 72.91 -> 80.93 with string mutation on, then 81 against the 83.79 the same tests score with it off. Never lower it to make a red run green. rollupBuilders.js finishes at 96.67 with two survivors that are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT rather than unexamined: both are the ' AND ' separator in `where.join(' AND ')` inside buildRolesAsRowsSql and buildRolesDrillSql, and each of those has exactly one `where.push` in its body, so the list can never hold two conditions and `[x].join(sep) === x` for every sep. They are left visible instead of silenced: the floor sits below them, so they cost nothing, and a future second condition would make them killable again -- which a disable comment would hide. scopeHistory.js followed, 51.66 -> 94.31. Remaining targets, both still on their first measurement: contextRollup.js (68.80) and attributeCut.js (70.93). src/lib/resourceVisibility.js joined this scope with #937: it is not under src/matrix, but it decides which resource types reach the matrix row axis at all, through the same buildSubqueries fragment as filterSql.js, and its second caller is the resources list -- a wrong answer there silently drops or duplicates whole rows. Its importers' tests (src/lib, src/routes/resources/) are in the include set for the same reason the route tests are. ATTRIBUTE LABELS JOINED THIS SCOPE (issue #872), not because they are matrix internals but because they are what the matrix's attribute picker, grouping headers and xlsx export TITLE their columns with, and because their importers' tests were already in this include: src/lib/attributeLabels.js is reached through routes/matrix.js, routes/resources.js and routes/permissions/**, and src/routes/attributeLabels.js is the endpoint the browser and the Power Query workbook both read. A wrong answer there is silent in the same way the rest of this scope is -- a label swapped in where the raw storage key was needed leaves a filter that used to work returning nothing, with nothing on screen to say so. They are also the reason vitest.stryker.matrix.config.js grew three test files; see the note there. FIRST MEASUREMENT 81.25 (lib) and 82.35 (routes), taking the scope to 83.48 against the 83.79 it scored without them -- the floor stays 81, which is where a ratchet is supposed to sit after a scope widens: the number moved because the denominator did, not because a test stopped discriminating. The lib file's remaining survivors cluster in its two five-minute caches (the TTL comparisons and the `target || '*'` cache key); the cross-target reuse and per-target keying now have tests, the TTL boundary itself does not. WHO CHANGED A SAVED MATRIX: src/routes/matrix/savedFilterHistory.js joined the mutate list. It turns the `_history` snapshots of a SavedMatrixFilters row into the trail the History dialog shows, and its decisions are the kind a mutant hides in plain sight: which columns are bookkeeping rather than changes (drop `updatedBy` from the skip set and every event reads "Updated By: anna -> wim" beside its own byline), that an update changing nothing a reader cares about produces NO event rather than an empty one, that a creation is credited to createdBy and a deletion to nobody, and which part of the matrix a changed filter key belongs to — a mutant that lets `rollupExpanded` fall through to the roll-up bucket makes "somebody expanded a group" read as "somebody re-cut the matrix", which is exactly the wrong person to go and ask. Its co-located test file is already inside this config's `src/routes/matrix/**` include, so it brings its own killers. This config disables StringLiteral/ObjectLiteral mutation, which suits it: the file also carries display labels, and mutating that prose would produce survivors that say nothing.

mutationExclusions.src/lib/systemFilter.js: Virtual `__system` filter column (#1204) for the Principals/Resources list pages. Listed in THIS config because it belongs to the same column-discovery/filter surface as lib/attributeLabels.js above, but excluded rather than mutated: what it decides is three small guards (schema-only vs fetched values, blank name -> null, no filter -> empty fragment), each pinned by its own case in src/lib/systemFilter.test.js; the rest of the file is the SQL text of an EXISTS against the real "Systems" table. Mutating that text would prove only that it is unchanged -- whether it selects the right rows is what contract-tests/systemFilter.contract.test.js answers against a real PostgreSQL schema, which is the same split already stated for src/routes/matrix/shares.js in stryker.auth.config.json.
mutationExclusions.src/contexts/plugins/system-membership.h: Shared body of the two system-membership context plugins (#1204). Recorded here only because a written exclusion has to live in a Stryker config and the context-plugin layer has none -- it is NOT part of this config's matrix scope, and every other module under src/contexts/plugins/ is grandfathered in .ci/js-mutation-scope-baseline.json. A dedicated stryker.contexts.config.json is the right home for it and cannot be added in isolation: tools/mutation/stryker_to_mutation_json.py derives the required report set from the configs, so a new config without a matching entry in the weekly workflow's hardcoded scope matrix would hard-fail the publish job. Its decisions (one context per distinct systemId, null member skipped, blank display name -> "System <id>", unsupported targetType rejected) are each pinned by a case in src/contexts/plugins/system-membership.test.js.
mutationExclusions.src/contexts/plugins/system-membership-p: Plugin descriptor for the principal side of system-membership (#1204) -- same placement caveat as system-membership.helpers.js above. Declaration only: a name/displayName/description/targetType, a parametersSchema object literal, and a one-line delegation to the shared helper. With this config's StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral mutators excluded there is no decision left in the file to mutate; the delegation is pinned by system-membership.test.js, which asserts the principal-side root name, targetType and that it reads the Principals table.
mutationExclusions.src/contexts/plugins/system-membership-r: Resource-side mirror of system-membership-principals.js -- identical shape, same reason.
